problem:
Given that the differential equation 

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+4\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-12y=12{x}^{2}-32x-30
$$

has the complementary function ${y}_{c}(x)=A{e}^{2x}+B{e}^{-6x}$, find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ to this equation.

activity_context.topic_title: Second-Order Inhomogeneous ODEs With Polynomial Forcing

feedback.problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}-10\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+25y=25{x}^{2}+5x-3.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the complementary function ${y}_{c}(x),$ which is the solution to the homogeneous equation

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}-10\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+25y=0.
$$

Writing down and solving the auxiliary equation gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}-10\lambda +25 & =0 \\ (\lambda -5)^{2} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So $\lambda =5$ is a repeated root, and therefore the complementary function ${y}_{c}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{c}(x)=A{e}^{5x}+Bx{e}^{5x}.
$$

We now need to find the particular integral ${y}_{p}(x).$

The right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is a polynomial of degree $2.$ Therefore, we assume that the particular integral is also a polynomial of degree $2,$ i.e.

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=\alpha {x}^{2}+\beta x+\gamma 
$$

where $\alpha ,$ $\beta ,$ and $\gamma $ are constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the first and second derivatives of ${y}_{p}$ gives:

$$
\frac{\text{d}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}x}=2\alpha x+\beta ,\,\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}=2\alpha 
$$

To find the values of $\alpha ,$ $\beta ,$ and $\gamma ,$ we substitute the derivatives into the differential equation. This gives:

$$
2\alpha -10(2\alpha x+\beta )+25(\alpha {x}^{2}+\beta x+\gamma )=25{x}^{2}+5x-3
$$

We then group the terms on the left-hand side, as follows:

$$
25\alpha {x}^{2}+(25\beta -20\alpha )x+(2\alpha -10\beta +25\gamma )=25{x}^{2}+5x-3
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}25\alpha =25\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\,{x}^{2}) \\ 25\beta -20\alpha =5\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\,x) \\ 2\alpha -10\beta +25\gamma =-3\, & (\text{equating the constants})\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $\alpha =1,\beta =1,\gamma =\frac{1}{5}.$

Therefore, the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{p}(x)={x}^{2}+x+\frac{1}{5}.
$$

The general solution is given by

$$
y(x)={y}_{c}(x)+{y}_{p}(x),
$$

and therefore, the general solution in our case is

$$
y=A{e}^{5x}+Bx{e}^{5x}+{x}^{2}+x+\frac{1}{5}.
$$
